turns.label: Clinician

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hi.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hi there. Can you just confirm your name, date of birth, and the first line of your address, first of all please?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. Uh, my name is Valerie Cole. My date of birth is the nineteenth of September, nineteen ninety three.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: My name's [inaudible] .

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: My address is, uh, sixty four, Cliveden Place, in, South Wimbledon.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Are you in a private place where you can have a confidential consultation today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes I am, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What can I do for you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I've been feeling really anxious over the past few months. turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you mind just telling me a bit more about, when it started? Do you think there's something which changed in your life at that time?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I guess so, I think um, I would say maybe about two months or so, I've been feeling like this, and that probably coincides with, me starting a new job, um. turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What's your job?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, so I work for a, a, a fashion retailer, in um, the head office team, and it's just a brand new sector. I've never worked in retail before, my boss is not very nice to me and I don't. And it's really impacting on like, on the rest of my life, like my sleep and stuff like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So, um, just day-to-day, tell me, from the start of your day, how it affects you. You said that you, you dread going to work. How, how does it affect you, in terms of like your sleep at night, and things like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Right. Yeah, this is really so, I, I, I've, as I say like, I don't want to go to work in the morning, so I just find no way of, I can't get out of bed. turns.text: OK. So what time, what time do you go to bed at night-time?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: About ten, eleven, probably.

turns.text: And what time do you get to sleep?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not for ages, I'm, I'm lying awake all night

turns.text: OK. And, when you eventually get to sleep, do you wake up with your alarm in the morning, or does something else wake you up, before then?

turns.text: Mmm. So I find my, my heart kind of racing, and then I'm just like panicking that I'm gonna be late, and that that's gonna make work even more stressful. turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, so how many hours sleep do you think you get a night?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: [inaudible] , I just, I can't even tell because I feel like I'm, even when I'm in sleep it's such a shallow sleep, but maybe, three, four hours, I'm getting now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, what about your eating patterns, any change in how you're eating, or whether you, your appetite's changed?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Probably, not, significant changes maybe. No I wouldn't say that, I wouldn't say that I'm eating like, much differently. Ohh that, I probably have more chocolate than normal, just because I feel, so down.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. You're eating regularly otherwise?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, [inaudible] .

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, you told me about the palpitations, just tell me a bit more about that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, So um, it's, it's usually kind of like, when I realise in the morning that, either um, I feel like I'm gonna be late, because I've like overslept 'cause I'm so tired. turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Does it feel like a regular fast beat, or an irregular, beat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Irregular, I think.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how long do you think it lasts for when you get it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ohh it can be anything, I think [inaudible] couple of minutes, or the other day I was actually just, sort of lying there for like, holding my hand on my chest for like ten minutes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Is that something that you've had before this, or is that a new thing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, but I would say this is only in the past. Sort of like, couple of months as I say that I've been, experiencing this.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any chest pain with that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, um, well yeah it's painful to [inaudible] , when the heart, when my heart is beating fast but, but, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, in the daytime, how, how, you said you, you're not getting much sleep so, how's your energy level in the daytime?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's just, really, really low, I mean I, I'm finding now that I'm just, I find no enjoyment at all. It's kind of day-to-day, and anything that I'm doing. It's not just my job it's, you know when I leave I'm just so tired that, anything that, previously was, really fun is just not, it's not enjoyable. And I'm [inaudible] like, yeah, on edge the whole time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So what do you do in the evenings?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well right now I'm, I'm working so late, and everything is really, really stressful. So I don't really get much time to myself but, when I do wanna go out, or, you know, see friends or just relax. It, it seems quite difficult to do that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and [inaudible] , are you avoiding contact with friends, or do you still see them?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I avoid them insomuch that I, feel like I'm. Yeah, so I mean sometimes it just, I know that I'm not gonna have fun, because I don't want to, go out and, do things that I would normally have done.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. What about, hobbies, or exercise, or anything else outside work? Do you do anything else outside work?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, as I say like everything that I had previously been doing has been, just difficult to continue with like, I did used to like to like go running, and. turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And have you, has it ever got so bad that you've actually had to miss work?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, 'cause I think that would just add to the tension, but I do like pretty much every morning I think, ohh I should call in sick or like, just not go.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, what's the worst that it's got? Have you ever, been, um, so overwhelmed that you couldn't, get in to the office, you couldn't, go into a situation? Have you ever had a panic attack?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: [inaudible] , um. No I wouldn't say so, I think, I've always managed to make it to work. But I, I wonder if it's building up. So this is why I wanted to call, [inaudible] I'm just worried it's building up to that, and I don't know what to do 'cause I have, feel it, felt it, get worse and worse over the past couple of months.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And apart from work, are there any other situations which evoke quite extreme anxiety, like being, in public places, social situations, public transport, anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah I mean, I find public transport really stressful anyway, especially being on the tube it's, 'cause it's quite, getting warmer so it's just really airless. Um, but I think the majority of it, 'cause my life is just so focused around work right now, the majority of it is focused around work as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Before this did you have any similar times in your life when you felt like this?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not really I, I'm, no, I would say. I mean everybody always has a bit of tension, a bit of anxiety but, I've never felt, anything this bad before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And what about your mood day-to-day? I mean, I can see that you're quite distressed by like that. Do you ever get really down about this?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. Um, I mean, yeah, yeah, 'cause I do, yeah. I'm pretty much, down like, I don't enjoy, being and not just my day at all 'cause. I'm just so worried about everything, um, and I find that even when I'm not, like even at the weekends and stuff it's just the, kind of like constant, feeling of just being a bit, down, a bit unhappy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: When do you think you last felt yourself?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um. I don't know, that's a good question, I can't really, I can't really put a [inaudible] on that at all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: [inaudible] . And has your mood ever been so low that you've felt like you just couldn't carry on with your job, or with your life, or with your normal, uh, things as they we're going on?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I wouldn't, no I wouldn't say that I've had, I haven't had any suicidal thoughts or any, thoughts that have been that extreme like, I haven't. You know I have, I have a good support system, like I do have good family and stuff. So I, I have, I don't have, uh worries about, actually wanting to, um, not go on. It's just that, I don't wanna go on like this.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah. OK. And where do you, who do you live with at home?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sorry?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Who do you live with at home?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I live with my parents, just my parents.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, and, how much alcohol do you have in an average week do you think?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, ooh I don't know, probably quite a lot on the Friday or Saturday, just because, that, that's kind of normal, um. Uh, maybe I, maybe I do have like a bit during the week. I guess I don't really keep track of it that much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So, how much would you, would you guess?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Probably like, probably quite a lot on a Friday or Saturday, because it's usually going out, so maybe like. I probably go over my limit just on those days, anyway, and then like, maybe a glass of wine during the week [inaudible] .

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you smoke or take any other drugs, or anything?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I try not to smoke, but I do, occasionally, but I don't take drugs.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you done [inaudible] , anything yourself to help? Have you [inaudible] , have you talked to anyone, talked to any counsellors? Done any, online, looked online at all? Any ways to [inaudible] ?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I, well I talk to my mum, because she also suffers from, well she's [inaudible] , suffered from like depression in the past. I didn't think that it was, that I was suffering from, actual depression because it just seems to be, manifesting as, as total [inaudible] , as just stress the whole time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: But um, I did talk to my mum about it but I haven't sought any, she recommended that I come to the GP, um, but I haven't sought any other.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And would you be happy to, have, some one-to-one therapy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah I think, yeah I think so. I've never done that before, but yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. I mean what we would suggest in the first instance is to, to. So you can self-refer via the NHS, for what we call like, talking therapy which is a type of inter-behavioural, where they can really look at your situation. How you're reacting to, the, [inaudible] , why, what's provoking anxiety, and what you can do, to try and overcome that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK. Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, so I can send you the link for that. Um, in the meantimes it can be a bit of a wait. There are some online resources that are really helpful. Um, can put the details, on there and you can, get on with them straight away and try and work through them as well.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh-huh.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, and if you're feeling like it's not helping at all, or your anxiety is getting worse, to the point where you can't cope with work, or you can't, just do your normal things day-to-day. Then, it's important for us to, for you to give us a call, back and just discuss that, further.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK. [inaudible] .

turns.text: I mean some people, with anxiety they, do need to take medication to control that but that's, not something that we'd suggest in the first instance.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.text: And I'll put some more information on your notes about, helping with your, sleep patterns and things like that.

turns.label: Patient
